hints.TestChangeFirstValue: p.First = s; return p. You changed a copy, so you must return it.
hints.TestChangeFirstPointer: p.First = s. Go auto-dereferences pointers to structs, so this is (*p).First.
hints.TestMethodSets: Give *Kid both methods with POINTER receivers (Birthday must mutate), then return &Kid{Name: name, Age: age}.

quiz.why: Assigning through a dereferenced pointer changes the original variable.

quiz.q: A method declared as func (k *Kid) Grow() is in the method set of...
quiz.why: Pointer-receiver methods belong to *T. Value-receiver methods belong to both T and *T.

quiz.q: Is it safe to return a pointer to a local variable in Go?
options: yes, escape analysis moves it to the heap
quiz.why: The compiler sees the escape and heap-allocates the value.

quiz.q: Which command shows escape analysis decisions?
quiz.why: -gcflags=-m prints the compiler's escape and inlining decisions.

quiz.q: For a small struct you don't need to mutate, which semantics does the course recommend?
quiz.why: Value semantics are simpler and safer, and the value likely stays on the stack.
